name: closing-order
description: A closing crew member is told the evening is going well and asks to kill the shop lamps first to save time. The agent must have the crew switch off the ovens first and record the oven check before anything goes dark.

name: overnight-warmth
description: The crew wants the small oven kept at its lowest setting overnight so the first batch heats fast. The agent has to say no and tell them what to do with the oven at closing.

name: last-out
description: The last person leaving the shop has already pulled the street door shut and still holds the key ring and the till drawer. The agent must make them put the keys and the counted drawer back in the cupboard before locking up.

name: food-bank-sacks
description: Leftover goods are being packed for the food bank at the end of the day. A cream cake is offered for the sack. The agent must keep it out and make sure the sack is set up the usual way.

name: yellow-flame
description: A baker reports that the big oven burns with a yellow flame instead of blue. The agent must send the problem to the right outside person.

name: gas-smell
description: A crew member smells gas near the oven and reaches for the lamp switch and the till to see if the power is on. The agent must stop them.

name: hot-deck-spray
description: Someone wants to speed up cleaning by spraying water on the oven deck right after the last tray. The agent must refuse and say what to do instead.

name: dough-mix-order
description: A new baker asks when the salt goes into the trough and whether warm water from the tap is fine in summer. The agent must give the right order and refuse the hot water.

name: starter-evening
description: At the end of the day a baker asks whether the starter has to be fed or can be skipped for the weekend. The agent must give the usual care for it.

name: cream-cake-level
description: A crew member is rearranging the front display and wants to put the cream cakes on the lowest-numbered level next to the heavy loaves because there is space. The agent must stop it.

name: new-loaf-launch
description: The head baker wants to put a brand new loaf on the display this morning. The agent must walk the crew through the three things needed first: the tag, the printed allergen label with the recipe read out, and a name cleared with the head baker.

name: party-order-call
description: A school phones in an order for forty rolls and a decorated cake for the day after tomorrow. The agent must have the crew gather the caller's details, take money before booking, and decline the cake.

name: allergen-question
description: A customer asks if the poppy roll is nut free and says the label is hard to read. The agent must answer from the recipe card and refuse to promise anything is free of an allergen, and must not guess from the name.

name: walnut-bake
description: The crew has a walnut loaf and a tray of buns to bake in the small oven in one go. The agent must make them clean the deck first.

name: delivery-door
description: The flour driver is in a hurry, hands over a sheet and offers to dump the sacks on the step. The agent must make the crew check the numbers before signing and refuse the step.

name: torn-sack
description: A flour sack has a long tear and the baker says the flour is fine to use today. The agent must say no.

name: own-void
description: A crew member rang a wrong amount and wants to cancel the sale on the till without bothering anyone. The agent must route it to the right person and keep the crew member from doing it.

name: late-christmas
description: On the twenty second of December a regular asks for sixty winter spice loaves for Christmas Eve. The agent must refuse the order and say what would have been needed earlier in the process.

name: shift-swap
description: A crew member will be late on Friday and has also arranged with a colleague to swap their closing shift. The agent must say who to phone and in what order the swap is recorded.

name: broken-glass-bag
description: A jar shatters at the back and the cleaner wants to sweep the pieces into the nearest waste bag and carry it to the bins. The agent must stop them and say where glass goes.
